title: Staged Graceful Shedder + Autoscaler Hint Protocol for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets occasionally enter high contention windows (bursty ingress, region outages, model switch events) that cause hard drops for small but latency-sensitive tenants. We need a deterministic minimum throughput floor negotiated with autoscaler hints and a staged shedder that degrades classes of traffic predictably rather than sudden all-or-nothing drops.

Goal: Implement a staged graceful shedder that: (1) exposes per-tenant min-throughput reservation which the admission layer enforces as a soft floor, (2) integrates a lightweight 'autoscaler-hint' protocol so the serving autoscaler can react earlier to sustained shed signals, and (3) provides explicit degradation stages (latency-first, quality-trim, best-effort) with telemetry and rollback. The feature must be compatible with Dedicated routing policies, tenant quotas, and existing fallback model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Admission layer can serve per-tenant min-throughput reservation and respect staged degradation policies under simulated contention
Autoscaler receives and records hint events (ShedStage=1..3) and adjusts desired instance count in a deterministic test harness
Fallback variant routing triggers when a tenant's min-throughput cannot be maintained and documented degraded responses are returned with correct headers
Benchmarked under 50%-200% load spikes showing smoother latency tail and reduced 5xx spikes compared to baseline
E2E rollout plan and runbook are reviewed and approved by SRE and Product
design_notes: Admission pipeline augmentation: add a lightweight staged-shedder node between router and ratequeue that evaluates tenant reservation vs available headroom

Staging semantics: Stage 0 = full (honor reservation), Stage 1 = latency-first shedding (background/low-priority requests delayed or queued), Stage 2 = quality-trim (apply top-k/temperature clamps or quantized model variant), Stage 3 = best-effort drop or redirect to lower-cost region
Autoscaler hint protocol: append ShedHint events to control-plane event stream with windowed counters and suggested target growth factor (1.0..2.0); hints are advisory and include confidence metric
Consistency model: reservations are soft; we avoid strict static reservations to prevent wasted capacity. Controller favors proportional fairness with guaranteed floor for eligible tenants.
tradeoffs: Soft reservations reduce wasted capacity but risk transient SLA misses for corner cases; tradeoff accepted to improve overall fleet utilization
Autoscaler hints introduce eventual coupling between serving and scaling loops; we limit frequency and use confidence smoothing to avoid oscillation
Staged degradation adds complexity to the admission pipeline and testing matrix but yields predictable customer-facing behavior instead of opaque 503s
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (API + telemetry): define ShedPolicy protobuf, wire event emission, add CI-only flag to enable hint propagation
Phase 2 (staging node): implement staged-shedder node and unit tests for decision logic. Add integration harness to simulate contention
Phase 3 (autoscaler integration): implement hint consumer in predictor service and validate decision curve in canary cluster
Phase 4 (rollout): start with internal beta tenants, then progressive canary across 3 dedicated fleets with monitoring and automatic rollback on error budget breach
test_plan: Unit tests for all stages and edge cases (reservation > available, zero-reservation tenants)
Integration tests: synthetic traffic generator injecting burst scenarios and slow downstream GPU simulator
Chaos tests: kill nodes to validate staged fallback and autoscaler reactions
Performance benchmarks: compare 95/99/99.9 latency and 5xx rate against baseline across 10k/s synthetic tenants
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: shed_stage_count{stage}, tenant_min_throughput_missed_ratio, shed_hint_emit_rate, hint_consumer_lag
Dashboards: per-fleet and per-tenant view showing reservation utilization and stage transitions
SLO alarms: alert when any canary's missed-throughput ratio > 0.5% for 10m or when autoscaler hint consumer lag > 30s
Runbook: documented rollback steps to disable stage escalation and drain hint emitter
rollout_plan: Week 0: feature gated deploy to staging; smoke tests and load harness validation
Week 1: enable in internal-beta fleet with 2 pilot tenants; collect telemetry and refine thresholds
Week 2-3: progressive canary across dedicated-10, dedicated-22 fleets with automated AB test comparing tail latency
Week 4: full opt-in release and enable default stage mapping for new tenants; monitor closely for 4 weeks
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Hint oscillation causing autoscaler thrash. Mitigation: smoothing window + min cool-down period + test harness validation
Risk: Incorrect stage mapping causing silent quality regressions. Mitigation: add response header X-Redwood-Shed-Stage and automated quality-checker on sample requests
Risk: Observability blindspots. Mitigation: include per-tenant auditing events and retention for 7 days during canary

2026-03-05: Autoscaler team implemented hint consumer stub; discovered need for confidence field to avoid false positives. Updated design notes.

2026-03-08: Internal load test: under 3x burst, staged shedding reduced 5xx spikes by 78% and improved 99p latency by 35% in stress lab. Seeing increased autoscaler hint emission; tuning smoothing windows next.
